findings.claim: ADR-023 §f, the new TODO debt row, era-label-bac-2006.json and prompts/010 all claim the item-5 check pins ALIAS_FROM["5"] and "goes red the day someone moves the constant without the fixture that justifies it" — it does not: the exact move the debt row contemplates (2005-12-01 -> 2004-03-15) leaves the entire gate and the self-check green.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-023-era-label-corrections.md:143 ("pinned as current behaviour by era-label-bac-2006.json's item-5 check, which goes red the day someone moves the constant"), repeated in tasks/TODO.md:70, evals/adversarial/era-label-bac-2006.json provenance, prompts/010-t14-taxonomy-completeness-and-10ka.md:137. The check is {"item":"5","field":"title","value":"Market for Registrant's Common Equity, Related Stockholder Matters and Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities"} on a fixture whose period end is 2006-12-31, so it only constrains ALIAS_FROM["5"] <= 2006-12-31 — it is blind to every earlier value, including the one §f argues is correct. segment.py's new _demo adds no date assert for item 5 either (only `"Common Equity" in item_label("5", date(1993,12,31))[1]`).
findings.repro: In the T14 worktree: set ALIAS_FROM["5"] = date(2004, 3, 15) in src/sec10k/segment.py, then `python3 -m evals.run --suite fast --no-report` -> 51/51 = 1.000, `python3 -m evals.run --suite invariant --no-report` -> 13/13 = 1.000, `python3 -m src.sec10k.segment` -> "[segment self-check] ok". (Only a move later than 2006-12-31 is caught: date(2007,1,1) -> fast 50/51.)
findings.acceptance: Either add a two-sided assert in segment._demo that pins ALIAS_FROM["5"] on both edges (as was done for 12/10/13/15), so the mutation above goes red, or restate the four claims to say what is actually pinned — an upper bound of 2006-12-31 and nothing else — and say plainly that no check can see a move in the 2004-03-15 -> 2005-12-01 direction.

findings.claim: ADR-023's Consequences assert that a wrong era label was invisible to every other check type — "no status, offset, confidence, warning or doc_status moves" — but the fix moves `confidence` from 0.75 to 0.95 on 10 item spans across 5 committed fixtures, and no eval case pins either the old or the new value.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-023-era-label-corrections.md:174 and the same claim in evals/adversarial/era-label-ge-1994.json triage ("No status, offset, confidence or warning moves — item_field is still the only check type that can see any of it"). Root cause: src/sec10k/validate.py:199 `base = BASE_STRICT if ev.get("title_similarity",0) >= 0.8 else BASE_WEAK`, and title_similarity is computed against TITLES aliases, which this diff edits. Measured main (f10bb6d) vs task/T14 over all 37 fixtures: ba-2003 items 12/13/15, gs-2002 item 15, ibm-1997 item 12, intc-2002 items 5/15, tgt-2002 items 12/13/15 all go 0.75 -> 0.95. Four of those five fixtures (gs-2002, ibm-1997, intc-2002, tgt-2002) have no new case at all, and their item titles change too.
findings.repro: For each fixture dir, run `src.sec10k.extract.extract_items(<primary file>)` on main and on task/T14 and diff items[*].confidence — e.g. ba-2003 item 15: 0.75 on main, 0.95 on the branch; fast stays 51/51 on both, proving no case reads the field.
findings.acceptance: Add at least one `confidence` check on an affected item (e.g. ba-2003 item 15 = 0.95, which would have been red pre-fix) and correct the ADR/case sentence so it no longer claims confidence is untouched by an era-label defect.

findings.claim: The new header comment on ALIAS_FROM states that every date in the table is written by a rule that keys on fiscal-period end "except '5'", which the same diff contradicts for "15" and ADR-023 §g contradicts for "6".
findings.evidence: src/sec10k/segment.py:133 ("Every date here keys on period end AND is written by a rule that keys on fiscal-period end too, except \"5\""). Three lines below, the "15" entry is 2004-05-23 because Release 33-8400 is an *effective-date* rule (ADR-023 §e: "adopted 2004-03-16, effective 2004-08-23") converted through the ADR-010 ruling-2 period-end compromise that ADDED["9B"] already carries; .claude/skills/sec10k-domain/SKILL.md writes it as "2004-05-23 (eff. 2004-08-23)". ALIAS_FROM["6"] = 2021-02-10 is likewise 33-10890's early-compliance/effective date, not a period-end key — ADR-023 §g says the period-end-keyed date is 2021-08-09. The adjacent claim "each one below now names the release it comes from" is also false for entries 4, 5, 6 and 14, which name no release.
findings.repro: Read src/sec10k/segment.py:127-152 against ADR-023 §e and §g; no code change needed.
findings.acceptance: The comment names the two entries that are period-end compromises rather than period-end rules (15 via 9B's convention, 6 via the early-compliance date), so a future maintainer does not read 2004-05-23 or 2021-02-10 as a rule date.

findings.claim: ADR-023's Pass-1 finding "every ADDED date is the right rule's" is qualified out of existence by §g and by the pre-existing 9B/9C entries, which are admittedly one-sided approximations rather than the rule's date.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-023-era-label-corrections.md, Context ("Pass 1 came back clean … every ADDED date is the right rule's") vs §g ("ADDED[\"7A\"] carries only the first date, so a small FY1997 registrant is expected to have an item it was exempt from") and src/sec10k/segment.py:75-95, where ADDED["9B"]=2004-05-23 and ADDED["9C"]=2021-10-01 are explicitly derived boundaries, not rule dates.
findings.repro: Read the two sections of ADR-023 side by side.
findings.acceptance: Pass-1's summary sentence is scoped ("every ADDED date derives from the right release; two are period-end approximations of filing-date rules and 7A carries one of two phase-in dates — see §g").
